status: Research-informed hypothetical demo specifications; no customer profiles or outcomes generated
methodology: Three selected paid peers per category; not all competitors or a representative market census.
Use one-time USD prices for physical products and short-term monthly USD costs for software. Exclude annual equivalents, human packages, free tiers, and cart promotions from those price medians.
Use independently sorted numeric fields; categorical baselines are common features or explicit design choices. No median invented for missing/unknown fields.
Store marketed standout and two deliberate disadvantages separately; final offers are median-derived concepts with stated exceptions, not literal all-field median products.
Customer-facing simulation offers must not expose negative/standout labels or this research rationale. Show factual attributes uniformly for all alternatives.
Known free/DIY and human substitutes remain choice options even when excluded from paid-peer arithmetic.
Manufacturer lumen/capacity claims and software feature claims are not independent performance tests.
Sony and CodeSensei remain unchanged; this research covers only the four newly selected scenarios.

proposed_products.name: Commuter backpack

baseline.Body dimensions: Approximately 45 × 30 × 17 cm; design choice, not componentwise median
baseline.Organization: Padded laptop compartment, front organizer, key clip, two bottle pockets
baseline.Carry: Padded shoulder straps and back panel
baseline.Fabric: Water-resistant polyester; no waterproof certification claimed
baseline.Warranty: Two years; design choice consistent with tomtoc sample

proposed_products.standout: Removable work organizer: lift out charger, cables, pens, and small essentials together and transfer to another bag. Organizer included.
proposed_products.selling_point: Switch bags without repacking your work essentials.

negative_features.comparison: Heavier than all three sampled bags (650–1,010 g); sample median 900 g.
negative_features.reason: A deliberate weight tradeoff to test against organizer convenience.

negative_features.feature: Laptop sleeve supports up to 15-inch devices; usable compartment 36 × 25 × 2.5 cm (proposed)
negative_features.comparison: Lower claimed diagonal compatibility than tomtoc 15.6-inch and 17.3-inch options; sample median 15.6 inches. Device dimensions still govern fit.
negative_features.reason: A deliberate compatibility limit; not a universal negative for smaller-laptop buyers.

proposed_products.design_notes: Price and capacity equal sample medians. Weight and laptop compatibility deliberately depart below competitiveness. Other categorical specifications are proposed common-feature choices, not computed medians.

proposed_products.name: Detachable desk lamp

baseline.Adjustment: Tilting head and adjustable desk stand
baseline.Controls: Physical power/brightness control; no app required
baseline.Charging: USB-C for detachable light; cable and USB power adapter included (proposed)
baseline.Battery target: Four hours at 100 lumens; full-output runtime unverified

proposed_products.standout: Detachable rechargeable light head that works on its included mini stand away from the desk base.
proposed_products.selling_point: One desk light that moves with your work.

negative_features.comparison: Below sampled median 420 lm and Lepro detailed specification of 750 lm; above IKEA 170 lm.
negative_features.reason: Deliberate light-output limitation, relevant to large work areas.

negative_features.feature: Fixed 2700 K warm-white light; no color-temperature selection
negative_features.comparison: OttLite offers three modes and Lepro five; IKEA is also fixed 2700 K.
negative_features.reason: Deliberate loss of color-temperature flexibility; may suit evening readers.

proposed_products.design_notes: Price equals sampled median. Brightness and color-mode count deliberately depart from sampled medians. Detachability and battery performance are unverified concept engineering targets. The three-brand price sample spans budget to premium; not a representative market median.

proposed_products.name: Job-targeted résumé review
proposed_products.price: $49/month, billed monthly; proposed from selected paid-software median

baseline.Scope: Up to two pages per résumé; one target job posting per review
baseline.Checks: Structure, clarity, bullet impact, formatting, and job-requirement coverage
baseline.Deliverable: Prioritized feedback plus suggested before/after bullet edits in a downloadable report
baseline.Method: AI-assisted analysis; no recruiter or human review promised
baseline.Boundary: No fabricated accomplishments and no interview or hiring guarantee

proposed_products.standout: Each suggested bullet rewrite includes the target-job requirement and the original résumé evidence it uses; missing evidence is flagged instead of filled in.
proposed_products.selling_point: See what each rewrite supports—and where the evidence comes from.

negative_features.comparison: Rezi advertises unlimited resumes; Resume Worded advertises unlimited complete reviews.
negative_features.reason: Deliberate usage cap at a median subscription price.

negative_features.feature: Delivery within 48 hours rather than instant feedback
negative_features.reason: Deliberate service delay; urgent applicants may prefer an immediate tool.

proposed_products.design_notes: $49 is the median of three selected monthly AI-software plans, not a per-review or human-service median. Page limit, deliverable format, cap, and delay are scenario design choices. Job tailoring already exists; traceable evidence is the proposed marketed emphasis, not proven exclusivity.

proposed_products.name: Explained document proofreading
proposed_products.price: $20 per document, one-time; retained proposed test price, NOT a computed median

baseline.Scope: One English document, up to 2,000 words
baseline.Deliverable: Edited document and an original/revised comparison
baseline.Tone: Preserve intended author tone; target promise, not measured performance
baseline.Method: AI-assisted editing; no human editor promised
baseline.Exclusions: No factual verification, citation verification, plagiarism certification, or subject-matter review

proposed_products.standout: An edit ledger explains each substantive change and distinguishes necessary corrections from optional style changes.
proposed_products.selling_point: Understand every meaningful edit. Keep control of your voice.

negative_features.feature: $20 for each document; no unlimited-document plan
negative_features.comparison: Scribbr AI advertises $9.95 for one month of unlimited documents; Grammarly and QuillBot also have free basic alternatives.
negative_features.reason: Deliberate recurring-cost disadvantage; keep rather than automatically improve the offer.

negative_features.comparison: Scribbr AI advertises at most ten minutes; free interactive correction tools are additional substitutes.
negative_features.reason: Deliberate delay to test whether explained edits justify waiting.

proposed_products.design_notes: Selected paid monthly-tool median is $19.95/month ($9.95, $19.95, $30). It cannot be relabeled $20/document. Common correction features form the baseline; the chosen billing unit and wait are explicit deviations. Document cap, file handling, and edit-ledger specifications are design choices.
